label: Instant-Payment Interoperability
description: Assess domestic instant-payment systems and mobile-money interoperability in emerging markets — switch design, ISO 20022 messaging, settlement and risk, regional rails (PAPSS, regional RTGS), with the consumer-redress and AML/CFT overlay.

claudeKnowledge.description: BIS CPMI Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (2012) and the CPMI/World Bank Payment Aspects of Financial Inclusion (PAFI) report; CPMI report on interoperability (Fast payments, multilateral platforms); ISO 20022 message catalogue (pacs.008 / pacs.002 / pacs.004 / pacs.028 / camt.054); national instant-payment scheme rules and switch operating manuals (Nigeria NIBSS NIP/NQR, Ghana GhIPSS GIP/GhanaPay, Kenya PesaLink/IPSL and the CBK National Payments Strategy, India NPCI UPI, Brazil Banco Central Pix, Tanzania TIPS, AfricaNenda SIIPS report); PAPSS (Pan-African Payment and Settlement System) rulebook and regional RTGS/RTGS-linkage arrangements (REPSS, SADC-RTGS / SIRESS, COMESA); FATF Recommendations (2023), FATF guidance on financial inclusion and AML/CFT, FATF Recommendation 16 (wire transfers); Level One Project / Mojaloop design principles; central-bank consumer-protection and dispute-resolution circulars; G20 Roadmap for Enhancing Cross-Border Payments.

guidedInputs.label: Known Issues or Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe known pain points: settlement-liquidity stress, failed-transaction backlog, redress complaints, AML typology concerns, interoperability disputes, or supervisory findings.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Reversal of failed P2P transfers takes 5+ days; deferred net settlement creates intraday exposure when a large participant misses a cycle; mobile-money wallets and bank accounts are not addressable on the same alias directory; rising APP/social-engineering fraud with no liability-allocation rule...

exampleInput: We operate a mobile-money business (~6 million active wallets) in a West African market and we are joining the national instant-payment switch as a direct participant next year. The switch runs on a deferred net settlement model with three cycles a day; we hold a prefunded settlement account at a sponsor bank. We are mid-migration from a proprietary ISO 8583-style message set to ISO 20022 pacs.008. Assess our readiness for interoperable bank-to-wallet and wallet-to-wallet transfers, focusing on settlement-liquidity risk, failed-transaction reversal and consumer redress, and the AML/CFT and travel-rule overlay for cross-network transfers. Known weak spots: our failed-transfer reversal SLA is informal and disputes are handled by email; we have no agreed liability-allocation rule for authorised push-payment fraud; and our alias directory cannot resolve a bank account and a wallet under the same phone number.

exampleValues.known_concerns: Failed-transfer reversal SLA is informal and disputes are handled over email with no logged audit trail. No agreed liability-allocation rule for authorised push-payment (APP) / social-engineering fraud. Alias directory cannot resolve a bank account and a wallet under the same MSISDN, so customers cannot pay across networks by phone number. Deferred net settlement creates intraday exposure if a large participant misses a cycle.
